title: What Actually Is RAM?
sources: Corsair, 'Volatile vs non-volatile memory: what's the difference?': RAM is volatile, short-term working memory that loses its data when power is removed; SSD/HDD storage keeps data with the power off

Kingston / Crucial 'memory vs storage' explainers and acemagic.com 'Memory vs storage': RAM holds the programs and data in use right now; storage holds files long term; RAM is far faster than an SSD, so programs are loaded from storage into RAM to run
Tom's Guide, 'Your computer is slow because the RAM is full': when RAM fills up, the OS moves data out to the page file / swap on the drive, which is much slower, so the computer slows down

Techlicious 'The power of restarting' and OnMSFT 'Why rebooting your Windows PC fixes many problems': a restart clears RAM and starts programs fresh, which fixes many glitches and slowdowns; unsaved work held only in RAM is lost when power is cut

lines.text: What actually is ram, and why does everyone want more of it?
Think of your computer as a desk.
Storage is the filing cabinet, where your files live for good,
lines.caps: *STORAGE IS | THE FILING *CABINET | WHERE YOUR *FILES | LIVE FOR *GOOD

lines.text: but ram is the desk, holding whatever you're using right now.
lines.caps: BUT *RAM | IS THE *DESK | HOLDING *WHATEVER | YOU'RE *USING | RIGHT *NOW

lines.text: The desk is way faster to grab from,
so every app you open gets copied onto it.
Open too many tabs and the desk fills up,
so stuff gets shoved back in the cabinet, and everything slows down.
lines.caps: SO *STUFF | GETS *SHOVED | *BACK IN | THE *CABINET | AND *EVERYTHING | *SLOWS DOWN

lines.text: But here's the catch: ram only remembers while it has power.
lines.caps: BUT *HERE'S | THE *CATCH | RAM ONLY *REMEMBERS | WHILE IT HAS *POWER

lines.text: Switch off, and the desk is wiped clean,
which is why unsaved work disappears,
and why a restart fixes so much.
